newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen off $0.50-$1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen off $0.50-$1 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Friday were seen $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt lower, pressured by continued light demand from packers with unprofitable operating margins, livestock dealers said.
Lower pork prices this week eroded operating margins, with packers losing an average of $5.00 to $7.00 per head, said Dave Maher, analyst with Securities Corp of Iowa.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top hog prices at the plant were seen $58.00 to $58.50 and Illinois top prices were seen at $57.00 to $57.50. Indiana/Ohio top hog prices to the plant were expected at $58.00 to $58.50, dealers said.
Pork product prices remained soft at midday, with fresh loins and butts weak, hams off $1.00 per cwt and pork bellies steady to $4.00 lower, USDA reported in its central U.S. carlot pork report.

The lower pork prices continued a trend started Monday. By Wednesday's close, the number two hog carcass cut-out value was quoted at $77.04, down $2.66 from Tuesday and down $4.39 since Friday, when the cut-out last traded higher, USDA statistics showed.
Cash hog price weakness also was tied to larger than expected hog marketings on Tuesday and Wednesday, they said.

Declines could be limited if the lower pork prices reawakens domestic retail demand or invites export business, market sources said. Lighter hog marketings as a new heat wave moves into the westner Corn Belt this weekend also could trim losses, the sources said.
